title: 1991 AMC 8 Problem 9
statement: How many whole numbers from \(1\) through \(46\) are divisible by either \(3\) or \(5\) or both?

solutions.text:
There are \(15\) multiples of \(3\) and \(9\) multiples of \(5\) up to \(46.\) The \(3\) multiples of \(15\) (namely \(15,\) \(30,\) \(45\)) were counted twice.

By inclusion-exclusion, the count is \(15 + 9 - 3 = 21.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: Count the multiples of \(3\) and the multiples of \(5\) separately
Numbers divisible by both \(3\) and \(5\) are multiples of \(15\) and get counted twice, so subtract them once
